methodology.calculations: Calculated observations retain formula, input observation IDs and original evidence. No interpolated revenue series, invented active-worker counts or undisclosed-margin estimates are presented as facts.
cohorts: Match period.type, period.year, currency, scope and accounting_basis before comparing revenue levels or calculating growth.
Annualized revenue is a dated pace, not recognized annual revenue or subscription ARR.
Whole-company, parent, AI Services and other-segment observations remain labelled separately.
Qualifiers are retained: greater_than/at_least are lower bounds, nearly is not an exact value, approximate remains approximate.
Missing disclosure is not zero and is not evidence that a business is unhealthy. Nonprofit research entities are not commercial vendors.
methodology.estimates: No new financial estimate is invented for missing data. A defensible future estimate must carry a range, explicit assumptions, date, scope and source inputs, and be switchable independently from reported observations.
methodology.freshness: Selected financial statements and company disclosures were read on 28 October 2026. Each source check records its outcome separately from the reporting period. Other observations retain the October 15 research review; a page retrieval does not verify every claim. A second primary-source pass added separately dated company operating statements and corrected estimate/accounting-basis classifications; unavailable revenue sources remain flagged.
methodology.selection: Supported canonical claims plus separately documented fresh source excerpts for new interim financial observations. New observations preserve their exact period, scope, units and source checks; the underlying canonical release is unchanged.

north_star.definition: Revenue from returning paying customers, less the direct cost of delivering their work, measured over a consistent period.
north_star.label: Gross profit from repeat customers
north_star.limitation: The reviewed sources do not disclose a comparable repeat-customer gross-profit series across this universe. No health score is assigned; the five signals and their gaps are shown instead.
north_star.why: It combines repeat demand with the value the company keeps after paying for delivery. Gross billings, funding and registrations can rise while the underlying business weakens.

signals.ideal_measure: Gross profit and gross margin; confirm with statutory profit and cash conversion.
signals.interpretation: Revenue can grow without profitable unit economics. A positive adjusted EBITDA figure can coexist with a statutory loss.
signals.label: Profit & margins
signals.limitations: Gross margin, statutory net margin, pre-tax profit and adjusted EBITDA have different definitions and are not ranked together.
signals.question: Does the company keep money after delivery?

signals.ideal_measure: Net revenue retention, repeat-customer share and largest/top-five revenue concentration.
signals.interpretation: Expansion and repeat spend are stronger evidence than a logo wall. Concentration exposes dependence on a few buyers.
signals.label: Customer durability
signals.limitations: Customer counts are explicitly labelled reach proxies. Named research partners, platform signups and unknown paid-status logos are not paying-customer counts.
signals.question: Do customers return, and how concentrated is demand?

signals.ideal_measure: Monthly paid active experts, accepted delivery hours/tasks, payout volume and utilization.
signals.interpretation: Paid throughput is closer to productive supply than a registered expert network.
signals.label: Paid delivery
signals.limitations: Daily snapshots, lifetime payouts and registered networks stay separate. No comparable monthly active paid-expert count is established in the reviewed records.
signals.question: Is the expert supply actually doing paid work?

signals.ideal_measure: Operating/free cash flow and months of runway from unrestricted cash divided by a defensible forward cash-burn estimate.
signals.interpretation: A growing business still needs liquidity. Employee counts describe delivery or cost capacity, not business health on their own.
signals.label: Cash & resilience
signals.limitations: Funding raised is not cash on hand. Net losses are not cash burn. Cash, net debt and company/team snapshots are separate context and do not establish runway.
signals.question: Can the business fund its next stage?

editorial_readouts.readout: Mercor has substantial institutional financing, a large expert supply network and a documented production evaluation stack. The strongest current operating evidence is its engineering disclosure of millions of weekly model evaluations; the billion-dollar headline is gross annualized customer spend. Reported period billings and fast growth establish material commercial activity, but retained economics and customer concentration remain opaque. Its March 2026 security incident adds a concrete diligence question about data handling and customer trust.

Snorkel combines an older software/data-development business with a much newer managed expert-data offering. Named production cases and a BNY agreement provide stronger commercial evidence than logos alone. Its September 2026 financing and $375M annualized run-rate show a major scale-up, but that number is company-reported and is neither audited full-year revenue nor demonstrated recurring software ARR. The investor story is increasingly about research-driven datasets and RL environments, not just weak-supervision tooling.

Handshake has a decade-old recruiting network and institutional backing, but its AI operation is a distinct new business. The near-$1B April 2026 run-rate is an investor-published operating claim, not an audited annual revenue figure. Cleanlab adds real research capability in evaluations and data quality. The obvious advantage is access to educated specialist talent; the public gap is named AI-data buyers, segment margins and a consistent dated revenue series. Historical parent funding and valuation should remain visible without being attributed to the AI division.

micro1's October 12 company update reports an annual run rate above $1B and confirms its Series B was priced at a $4B valuation. These are company statements, not audited annual revenue; gross/net and pre/post-money bases are unspecified. Primary financing size is undisclosed, and the approximately $25M employee tender is secondary liquidity. The previously disclosed $1B enterprise-data spending plan remains separate from revenue and financing.
editorial_readouts.segment: Expert data, environments and agent evaluation

editorial_readouts.readout: Scale has the strongest combination here of long-lived delivery examples, a buyer-confirmed government award, major financing and a large reported revenue base. It now spans data, evaluations, enterprise applications and public-sector systems, so reducing it to an annotation marketplace is misleading. Meta’s investment changed its ownership and commercial context and included substantial shareholder liquidity. The latest public update emphasizes bookings and applications growth; it does not supply an audited 2025 revenue amount.

Turing combines expert training data and environments with enterprise AI deployment. Its January 2025 company release describes a $300M annual revenue run rate at 2024 year-end; that measure is annualized, not recognized full-year revenue or recurring SaaS ARR. Its March 2025 financing and later enterprise offering provide additional operating context, while current audited revenue and segment economics remain undisclosed.

Labelbox now spans Recursion enterprise agents, Horizon RL environments, Terra robotics data and Alignerr expert signals. Its October 14 Series E announcement discloses more than $100M in equity at a $1.25B pre-money valuation, with a separate unsized credit facility. The earlier approximately $189M funding total is historical, not a current lifetime total; current revenue and margins remain undisclosed.
editorial_readouts.segment: Enterprise agents, RL environments and expert data

editorial_readouts.readout: Scaled compute and reinforcement-learning infrastructure provider with issuer-reported company-wide annualized revenue above $100m and a substantive named Ramp deployment case. Commercial proof is strong for the platform, but it does not establish a $100m expert-data business, SaaS ARR, disclosed margins or independently replicated task performance.

Early expert-data supplier with company-reported lab engagements, expert capacity and recurring token output. These are meaningful delivery signals, but anonymous buyers and no disclosed contract values or verified revenue leave commercial scale and repeatability unproven.

Expert datasets, RL environments and enterprise model services, with NVIDIA-confirmed task use and Legora-confirmed evaluation collaboration. The $30M Series A was announced April 9 after closing months earlier; >$100M annualized revenue run rate was disclosed that day, with the crossing date unknown. The later $3.2B valuation is a Forbes report, repeated in some job copy; financing size, exact close and valuation basis remain undisclosed.
editorial_readouts.signal: NVIDIA confirms AfterQuery task use; payment terms undisclosed

editorial_readouts.readout: Research-led supplier with demonstrated enterprise delivery and named counterparty collaboration. Snowflake strengthens external validation beyond the supplier-side Intuit case; commercial scale remains undisclosed. Stronger evidence of technical credibility than of recurring revenue.

Credible early specialist with relevant post-training/systems founders, institutional backing and a concrete multi-tool benchmark. Current evidence supports an operating environment supplier and research capability; neither buyer validation nor repeatable commercial scale has yet been publicly demonstrated.

The commercial outlier in this subgroup: a dated, company-reported $200M run rate supported by substantial infrastructure and a transaction-adviser-confirmed seed. Treat it as rapidly scaled but financially opaque; missing named buyers, concentration and revenue-recognition details limit valuation comparisons.

Buyer-validated AI-safety evaluation specialist. A commissioned Anthropic engagement and Meta-confirmed benchmark delivery establish genuine external use with unusually strong primary evidence. Financial scale and repeat-contract economics remain opaque; do not equate undisclosed funding with lack of traction.

Early reinforcement-learning environment and post-training supplier with clearly articulated technical ownership, verifier design and expert-quality processes. Public evidence reviewed establishes the offering and team capability, but not a named paid deployment, revenue scale or repeat purchasing.

Established, large-scale expert-data and post-training supplier with buyer-side delivery evidence from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta. Founder currently reports no outside funding. Reported 2024 revenue above $1B is strong independent journalism, not an audited public revenue series; financing talks and wealth-based valuations must not appear as closed funding.
editorial_readouts.signal: Over $1B FY2024 revenue reported by Reuters

editorial_readouts.readout: An experienced systems team undertaking a new agent-analytics launch after limited conversion in its prior database business. Hydrolix validates historical technical value, but that asset sale does not validate current AI revenue. Track as an adjacent analytics/evaluation entrant, not an established current frontier-data vendor.

A commercially active coding-data supplier, not merely a visible offer: dated lead-investor disclosure identifies substantial signed contracts and actual contributor payouts. Product breadth and DeepSWE show continued technical output. Current revenue, margins, valuation and retention remain unverified; old recruiting claims deserve labels, not erasure.

Benchmark and agent-environment specialist with concrete open research assets and a founder whose evaluation experience fits the product. Public product adoption and fundraising do not yet establish named paid customers, contract economics or repeatable commercial delivery.

An established engineering talent business extending into frontier-lab RLHF work, with reported staffing capacity and expert payouts indicating operating activity. The reviewed evidence does not isolate current AI-data revenue, identify confirmed lab buyers or turn historical hiring revenue and ambiguous payout figures into current annual sales.

A.Team's current offer centers on agentic AI systems built and operated inside customer workflows by embedded engineers, with a continuing technical-talent business. Its network and historical engagement metrics describe delivery capacity; they do not measure recurring software revenue or a standalone frontier-data business.
editorial_readouts.segment: Embedded AI systems and engineering services

editorial_readouts.readout: Established developer-assessment and hiring platform now offering expert code data, reinforcement-learning gyms and private benchmarks through HackerRank Bench/Astra. Its broad developer community and hiring customer base support distribution and sourcing capacity, but are not proof of paid frontier-lab data customers or AI-data revenue.

Expert-data services provider with unusually strong buyer-side evidence: a UK AI Security Institute paper names Pareto as its commercial partner and documents delivered expert recruitment, rubrics and grading. This establishes a substantive completed engagement; fees, renewals, current contract status and scalable recurring revenue remain undisclosed.

Early specialized data-sourcing provider with strong but issuer-reported commercial signals: revenue well above seven figures and signed frontier-lab contracts in eight figures. Missing currencies, periods and recognition terms prevent treating these as ARR or recognized revenue; named buyer-side confirmation and delivery repeatability remain limited.

Well-funded visual-reasoning model developer with an accomplished research team, not a third-party data-labeling supplier. Public model access remains waitlisted as of this review; no production revenue or named paying customers were established. Funding is evidence of financing, not product-market fit.
editorial_readouts.segment: Adjacent foundation-model builder / potential data buyer
editorial_readouts.signal: $55M financing announced Apr 2026; public model forthcoming

editorial_readouts.readout: Expert-task and AI-data marketplace with company-reported expert payouts, delivered work hours and opportunities, which are more concrete operating signals than registered-network size alone. The reviewed public sources do not establish revenue, take rate, named paying labs or repeat contract economics.

Research institution and open infrastructure sponsor with credible benchmark adoption and company-reported grant deployment. Its research contribution is substantive, but grants, philanthropic pledges and benchmark users do not establish a commercial data-vendor business or justify a commercial maturity stage.

Invisible has a meaningful revenue business rather than only a talent network: the company disclosed $134M of FY2024 sales, and a detailed Cohere case describes expert evaluation work. Its opportunity spans model development and enterprise automation, making it broader than a labeling vendor. The analytical trap is to treat all its activity like recurring software revenue or all ownership transactions like startup funding. Its operating model combines people, processes and software; debt-funded buybacks and secondary transfers are distinct from the $100M announced primary financing. Current-year growth, revenue mix, gross margins and concentration still need disclosure before assuming SaaS-like economics or extrapolating its historical expansion.

Toloka has credible current technical adoption: Shopify describes its experts inside an ongoing production-learning loop, a materially stronger signal than a logo wall. Its business has also changed substantially from its legacy crowdsourcing origins toward GenAI expert data. Public parent filings reveal a real but historically much smaller business than some unsourced market profiles suggest: roughly $26M of FY2024 revenue, with significant losses then. The 2025 investment changed voting control while Nebius retained most economic exposure. Subsequent revenue is not publicly comparable after deconsolidation, so neither a 2025 stub nor a financing amount should be used to imply today’s commercial scale.

Established verified-participant platform with substantial AI-data delivery. The CEO reports $300M+ annualized revenue in spring 2026 and a $10M revenue week; these are company claims with unresolved gross-versus-net basis, not audited annual revenue. The prior profile materially understated commercial scale by omitting them.

Nonprofit-sponsored research project focused on foundational intelligence research, with relevant academic leadership. No reviewed public evidence establishes a commercial expert-data marketplace, paying customers or revenue; assess its research role separately from commercial suppliers.

Appen is the most financially transparent of these four and should be assessed as a listed operating-business turnaround. Its latest reviewed half-year shows renewed aggregate growth, but the geography matters: rapid China expansion offsets a shrinking Global segment. It supplies genuine GenAI training and evaluation work and has established delivery infrastructure, yet revenue remains concentrated and positive adjusted EBITDA does not mean statutory profitability. Its historical Google relationship must not be shown as current. Compare its disclosed service revenue with other companies on a like-for-like basis; fundraising, ARR estimates and annualized monthly run rates are poor substitutes for Appen’s actual reported sales.

Enterprise AI evaluation and security software/services vendor with named enterprise testimony and a defined subscription offering. Public evidence supports commercial product use, but supplier-hosted cases and undisclosed financials do not establish recurring-revenue scale, contract values or retention.

Enterprise AI alignment and compliance tooling vendor with named supplier-hosted customer testimony and concrete model/product delivery. Funding and grant-supported research strengthen execution capacity, but disclosed evidence does not establish revenue scale, contract economics or recurring customer retention.

Japanese training-data and annotation supplier with a detailed named customer interview documenting paid outsourcing, production use and reported outcomes. This is solid project-delivery evidence; its newer physical-AI collection site expands the offering, while revenue scale and repeat commercial adoption of that newer product remain undisclosed.

Established AI-data services operation inside a listed, diversified language and technology group, with issuer regulatory reporting describing actual TrainAI growth and client work. Group and Generate-segment financials are substantive commercial evidence, but cannot be assigned wholly to TrainAI or used to infer standalone data-services revenue or margins.

Buyer-confirmed production work and a documented account expansion support repeatable delivery. Its preliminary unaudited standalone revenue was approximately $59m for the twelve months ended March 31, 2026; GenAI-only revenue and named frontier clients remain undisclosed.
editorial_readouts.segment: Established human-data and annotation specialist; acquired strategic platform

editorial_readouts.readout: Named production deliveries and several years of commercial work support an established broad data-services business. Current named frontier-model exposure is not established; OpenAI work ended in 2022 and the reviewed Meta relationship ended in April 2026.
